bib.title: Think Bayes, ch. 4: More Estimation
bib.venue: book chapter (Think Bayes, 1st ed., Green Tea Press / O'Reilly, 2012; no journal)

question: What does a posterior over a coin's bias say, and how far do different priors matter once there is data?

results.claim: Euro coin spun 250 times came up heads 140 times; on a uniform prior over 101 hypotheses the maximum-likelihood value is 56.
results.quote: In this case the result is 56

results.claim: Posterior mean 55.95 and median 56 for the Euro problem.
results.quote: The mean is 55.95; the median is 56.

results.claim: The 90% credible interval is (51, 61), which excludes 50%.
The posterior probability of exactly x=50 is 0.021 but is almost meaningless because it depends on how finely the range is divided.
results.quote: The result is 0.021, but that value is almost meaningless.

results.claim: A triangular prior gives identical medians and credible intervals and means within 0.5% of the uniform-prior ones: priors are swamped.
results.setup: triangular prior peaking at 50, same 250 spins
results.quote: the means differ by less than 0.5%

results.claim: Beta(alpha, beta) is conjugate to the binomial: posterior is Beta(alpha+h, beta+t); Beta(1,1) is uniform and the Euro posterior mean is 56%.
results.quote: the posterior is a beta distribution with parameters alpha+h and beta+t

results.claim: Cromwell's rule: never give a prior probability of 0 to a hypothesis that is even remotely possible, since the posterior stays 0 regardless of data.

limits: Convergence claim is illustrated with one pair of priors on one dataset.
practices: Summarise a posterior with MLE, mean, median and a credible interval, and do not read a single grid point's probability as a hypothesis probability (p.35).
Test sensitivity with a second prior; with enough data posteriors converge (p.36).
Process the whole dataset in the likelihood (heads, tails) rather than one spin at a time; use the conjugate Beta update when it fits (p.38-39).

terms.definition: with enough data, people who start with different priors will tend to converge on the same posterior
the recommendation that you should avoid giving a prior probability of 0 to any hypothesis that is even remotely possible

lineage.work: MacKay, Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
